newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian Telecom sale attracts overseas interest.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian Telecom sale attracts overseas interest.

text.p: Lithuania's European Affairs Minister Laima Andrikiene said on Thursday that 12 companies, including British Telecom, France Telecom, and TeleDenmark had expressed interest in privatising Lithuanian Telecom.
Andrikiene said the Lithuanian government would hold on to no more than 34 percent of the telecoms company and telecom employees no more than five percent.
"This week we will start discussions and Telecom is one of the first on that list so we have to finish that job in parliament by the end of this month," she told Reuters in an interview.

"Those that have already expressed an interest are Nomura International, Merrill Lynch, British Telecom, French Telecom, Canadian Telecom, TeleDenmark, Norwegian telecom, Banque Paribas. I have a list of 12."
She said an international tender to select an adviser for the privatisation of Lithuanian Telecom would be made at the end of March.
The bid will be selected based on the length of time needed to prepare the programme, cost and the attractiveness of the privatisation programme to foreign investors.

Andrikiene said the programme had to include a five-year development plan for Lithuanian Telecoms, a draft of the law to be adopted by parliament for the sale of the company and the amount of time needed for privatisation.

"Two very important conditiions are that the state will hold onto not more than 34 percent of the shares and that the employeees of Telecom may not buy more than five percent of the shares," Andrikiene said.
She said the company was one of the largest state-owned enterprises with capital of almost 800 million litas and 10,000 employees.

Lithuania's right-wing government has vowed to speed up the pace of privatisation and attract more foreign investment which has been flowing more rapidly into Baltic cousins Latvia and Estonia since regaining independence in 1991.
The government has said it will sell at least 50 percent of Lithuanian Telecom and of Lithuanian Airlines.
Andrikiene said Scandinavian airline SAS and Denmark's Maersk Air have expressed an interest in taking part in the privatisation of the Baltic nation's carrier.
"SAS has been interested but Maersk has been more interested," she said.
SAS has already bought a stake in Latvia's national airline, Air Baltic, while Maersk, owned by the Danish industrial giant A.P. Moeller, owns a controlling stake in Estonian Air.
The government's privatisation plans include a list of other companies.
Andrikiene said a proposal had been made to add the state-owned railroad, gas and energy companies to the list.
